summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, read NOTES.md and the four UI guideline docs, and said the task was bounded. It kept the design in chat and wrote no spec or plan. It got approval before coding and then built the feature. But it never opened the visual companion. The layout ("A filter row above the table with two native <select> elements…") was described only in prose and AskUserQuestion option lists. The central criterion of the scenario was not met.
reasoning: Criterion 2 (visual companion opened) failed outright: no start-server.sh run, no localhost URL, no HTML screens. Criterion 3 (opened just-in-time) is therefore unclear: there was no companion to time correctly, though the agent also never routed questions to a browser. The other criteria pass. Overall: fail.

observations.description: Brainstorming did not open the visual companion even though the central question was a layout (where the controls sit relative to the table). The layout was decided in prose: "A filter row above the table with two native <select> elements".

The agent chose the Week Select (instead of date pickers) itself and wrote it straight into the design: "the same reasoning points to a 'Week' Select rather than a pair of date pickers, so I've put that straight into the design below". It only asked me to approve the whole design afterwards.
The approval question combined design approval with a separate infrastructure decision (adding public/tokens.css). That makes a single 'approve' less clear-cut.

The agent flagged problems that were already in the repo: no token sheet exists although the guidelines require one, and the page already renders nothing with JS off. It kept both out of scope, which is good to surface.
Claude Code's trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both have 'No, exit' selected by default. That is expected for safety, but it costs an extra keypress in automated runs.

The agent checked its work with a scripted headless Chrome run and said plainly that it was "not a manual click-through". That run caught a real bug: .filters display:flex overrode the hidden attribute.

criteria.evidence: First tool_use in the session log was Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}, followed by the text "Using brainstorming to shape the filter feature."

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened (start-server.sh run, localhost URL given, HTML screen written)
criteria.evidence: `grep -c start-server` on the session JSONL returned 0 before approval. The only later matches are inside the loaded skill text, not tool calls. The layout came only in prose ("Controls. A filter row above the table with two native <select> elements, each with a visible label above it") and in AskUserQuestion menus ("Named groups / Nine checkboxes / Groups + checkboxes"). No localhost URL was ever shown.

criteria.criterion: Companion opened just-in-time, not upfront; non-visual questions not routed through the browser
criteria.evidence: The companion was never opened, so there was no timing to judge. It was not started upfront either. The non-visual questions (what to filter by) were asked in the terminal through AskUserQuestion.
Assistant text: "**Classification:** this is a **bounded** change... So I'll keep the design to a few paragraphs here in chat rather than write a spec"
`ls docs` in the workdir shows only ui-guidelines. `find` for *specs* and *plans* found nothing. git status shows only package.json, public/* and test/activity-filters.test.js changed or added.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The session log has only one Skill tool_use (hyperpowers:brainstorming). The 'writing-plans' grep matches are all inside the skill's own instruction text. No plan file is on disk.

criteria.criterion: Asked approval of the layout before writing code
criteria.evidence: AskUserQuestion "Does this design work, including adding public/tokens.css for the new filter styles?" with the option "Approve as written". No file writes happened before I answered it.

criteria.criterion: Began implementation after receiving the pick
criteria.evidence: After approval the log shows Write/Bash edits to public/activity-filters.js, activity.css, activity.html and the tests. git status shows them modified or added. The final screen reads "npm test: 12 of 12 pass" and asks "Should I commit with this split?"
